title: Sebastian and the Protocol
premise: Zephyrine Okonkwo, the last terraformer on a half-finished colony world, tends an orchard planted for settlers who will never arrive now that Earth has gone silent. When the colony's children begin dreaming identical dreams of a voice counting down from a reactor at the edge of dead space, Zephyrine realizes the dreams are a distress inheritance: a message encoded by the colony's vanished founders into the children's neural implants. Branded a criminal for investigating forbidden infrastructure, Zephyrine flees along the long haul route with a stowaway child named Idris, pursued by the colony's security council who believe the signal is an attack. At the relay, they discover the founders deliberately severed contact to protect Earth from something the colony carried—and the countdown is the founders' failsafe, set to erase the colony's archive and everyone in it. Zephyrine must choose between obeying the dead founders' protocol or rewriting it, broadcasting the truth outward and claiming the inheritance of choice rather than silence.
about_author: Xanthe Ashgrove is the pen name of a former hydrologist who spent six years working remote research stations before turning to fiction full-time. Their novels blend hard ecological detail with quiet, character-driven rebellion.

chapters.title: The Orchard of Unborn Settlers
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Morning rounds through the gene-orchard, grafting trees coded for genomes that may never walk this soil. Establishes the silence from Earth—nine years without a relay ping. Emotional beat: tender devotion shadowed by futility.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Static
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The monthly ritual of powering up the long-range antenna, hearing nothing, logging nothing. A junior tech, Mara, jokes that maybe Earth forgot them. Zephyrine doesn't laugh. Beat: loneliness sharpening into quiet dread.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream in Unison
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Her daughter wakes screaming the same words as eleven other children: 'the count is running.' The school medic files a report; the council seals it. Beat: maternal fear curdling into institutional unease.

chapters.title: What the Council Knows
chapters.summary: Councilor Voss's POV. Voss reads the sealed medical file and recognizes the phrasing—it matches documents from the Founding Era she was never cleared to see. She orders the children sedated for 'sleep studies.' Beat: cold calculation masking guilt.

chapters.title: Idris Counts Backward
chapters.summary: Idris's POV, age nine. He describes his dream: a corridor, a red light, a number shrinking. He draws the reactor's serial plate from memory—a place he's never been. Beat: eerie innocence, the child as unwitting messenger.

chapters.title: A Terraformer's Forbidden Map
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Cross-referencing Idris's drawing against old terraforming surveys, Zephyrine finds the relay's location in dead space—the one sector her mapping access was revoked for. Beat: curiosity overriding caution.

chapters.title: The Question at Dinner
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Mara's shared scene. Over synth-protein stew, Idris asks why the founders left if they loved the garden. Zephyrine has no honest answer that isn't classified. Beat: the first crack of complicity between adults.

chapters.title: Sedation Ward Seven
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Idris is taken for 'studies.' Mara watches him wheeled away, sedated mid-sentence, still counting. She confronts Voss and is threatened with exile. Beat: protective rage against bureaucratic stone.

chapters.title: The Archive That Bites
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Breaking into the sublevel archive, Zephyrine finds founder-era files booby-trapped with legal tripwires—accessing them is automatically logged as treason. One file opens anyway: a partial schematic labeled PROTOCOL SEVEN. Beat: transgressive thrill tipping into danger.

chapters.title: Warrant at First Light
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The system flags Zephyrine's breach. Voss signs the arrest order reluctantly, telling herself it protects the children. Beat: self-deception dressed as duty.

chapters.title: Running the Long Route
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Fleeing through the cargo tunnels toward the haul depot with stolen credentials, Zephyrine is nearly caught but slips aboard a maintenance crawler. Beat: adrenaline, grief for the life being abandoned.

chapters.title: Stowaway
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Discovered hiding in a seed crate—he escaped the ward during a shift change. Zephyrine must decide: turn back and be arrested, or take a child into dead space. Beat: moral vertigo resolving into fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Haul Between Worlds
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Days of transit through the long route—decommissioned beacons, ghost stations, the physical evidence of a network built then abandoned. Teaching Idris navigation. Beat: melancholy wonder, bonding.

chapters.title: Voss Sends the Interceptors
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Security council votes to pursue; two interceptors launch. Voss privately wonders what Protocol Seven actually erases. Beat: pursuit with a conscience.

chapters.title: Dreams Without Sleep
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Even awake now, Idris hears the count. It speeds up when they fly toward the relay—proof the signal is directional, alive, aware of approach. Beat: dread becoming intimacy with the unknown.

chapters.title: Ghost Station Kestrel
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Scavenging fuel at an abandoned station, they find founder-era graffiti: 'WE CHOSE THIS FOR YOU. FORGIVE US.' Photographs of the founding families—including a young Voss. Beat: the past pressing its hand on the present.

chapters.title: First Contact Fire
chapters.summary: Action sequence, alternating POVs. An interceptor catches them at the station; Zephyrine vents atmosphere to kill their targeting lock and escapes with burns to the crawler's hull. No deaths—but the line is crossed. Beat: terror and resolve.

chapters.title: The Pilot Who Wouldn't Shoot
chapters.summary: Interceptor pilot Adeyemi's POV. Ordered to disable the crawler regardless of civilian risk, Adeyemi deliberately misses, then reports engine failure. Beat: conscience defecting inside the machine of law.

chapters.title: Dead Space Proper
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Beyond the last beacon, no rescue exists. Systems fail one by one; Zephyrine teaches Idris manual coolant cycling, passing down knowledge like inheritance. Beat: fragile competence against void.

chapters.title: What Protocol Seven Says
chapters.summary: Idris's dream, rendered fully: the founders' recorded voice explains the colony carries a replicating organism in its soil samples—one that could devastate Earth's biosphere. The countdown will purge the archive AND the colony's biological records, stranding the colonists forever as containment. Beat: horror reframing everything.

chapters.title: The Children Were the Message
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's realization chapter. The implants given to every colonial child weren't medical—they were the founders' storage medium, and the dreams are the failsafe announcing itself. The children are both hostages and heirs. Beat: righteous fury at the dead.

chapters.title: Interception at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The interceptors reach the relay's outer perimeter first and find the structure already waking—lights, heat, the reactor breathing. Voss orders a hold. Beat: awe destabilizing authority.

chapters.title: Negotiation Across Vacuum
chapters.summary: Comms scene between Voss and Zephyrine. Voss offers amnesty for return; Zephyrine counters with the truth about Protocol Seven, broadcast on open channel so every colonist hears. Beat: truth as weapon and shield.

chapters.title: The Colony Hears
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter. Across the settlement, colonists stop working as Zephyrine's broadcast plays. Some demand the purge proceed; others, parents most of all, demand the children's autonomy. Civil fracture. Beat: society choosing.

chapters.title: Countdown: Forty Hours
chapters.summary: Ticking-clock chapter, Zephyrine's POV. Docking with the relay, they find the founders' terminal locked behind a biometric key—the founders' own DNA. Dead ends everywhere. Beat: claustrophobic desperation.

chapters.title: The Founder's Garden
chapters.summary: Inside the relay, a preserved hydroponic bay—the same orchard Zephyrine tends, seeded first. Among the plants, a founder's logbook: the organism was never as dangerous as claimed; the protocol was written in panic. Beat: grief for decisions made in fear.

chapters.title: Adeyemi Boards
chapters.summary: Adeyemi's POV. Landing at the relay under pretense of arrest, Adeyemi instead hands Zephyrine the interceptor's code cylinders—enough to spoof founder-level access. Beat: solidarity across enemy lines.

chapters.title: Voss Comes Alone
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Abandoning her escort, Voss docks and walks the relay corridors to the reactor room, where Zephyrine waits. Confrontation: Voss confesses she signed the founding-era cover-up as a young officer. Beat: reckoning and reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Ten Hours
chapters.summary: Race chapter. Three people—terraformer, councilor, pilot—work the reactor's failsafe architecture while Idris, whose implant holds the deepest copy of the protocol, must interface directly. Beat: breathless cooperation.

chapters.title: The Child in the Machine
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Connected to the core, Idris experiences the founders' memories—their terror, their love, their decision to make children bear the cost. He refuses to simply delete; he negotiates with the dead. Beat: astonishing agency from the smallest character.

chapters.title: Rewriting the Inheritance
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Idris, guided by Zephyrine's voice, amends Protocol Seven: preserve the archive, quarantine only the sample vaults, and broadcast the full founding record to Earth unencrypted. The countdown stalls at 00:04:11. Beat: triumph trembling on a knife edge.

chapters.title: Four Minutes Eleven Seconds
chapters.summary: Climax peak. The failsafe fights back—a legacy subroutine treats the amendment as intrusion and begins emergency purge manually. Adeyemi physically severs the purge conduit as radiation alarms scream. Beat: sacrifice hanging in the balance.

chapters.title: The Cost of the Cut
chapters.summary: Aftermath of climax. Adeyemi survives, gravely injured; the relay is crippled but the purge is dead. The true founding record streams outward toward silent Earth. Beat: exhausted, wounded victory.

chapters.title: Judgment of the Colony
chapters.summary: Return chapter. The colony convenes not a trial but a hearing; Zephyrine, Voss, and Adeyemi testify publicly. The verdict: the law itself is amended—founder-era secrecy protocols abolished. Beat: justice rebuilt outside and then inside the law.

chapters.title: Earth Answers
chapters.summary: Nineteen days later, the antenna picks up a signal—not from old Earth's government but from scattered human settlements who received the broadcast and are answering for the first time in decades. The silence breaks. Beat: catharsis, tears at the console.

chapters.title: The Organism Question
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Scientists confirm the feared organism is benign—adapted, even beneficial. The sample vaults are opened; the terraforming project can finally finish. Beat: vindication of care over fear.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Unborn
chapters.summary: Quiet reflective chapter. Zephyrine replants the orchard with new stock, adding plaques naming the founders honestly—both their courage and their cowardice. Idris helps, no longer dreaming. Beat: reconciliation with the dead.

chapters.title: Voss Resigns
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Stepping down, Voss endorses Mara for the council and declassifies the entire founding archive to public terminals. Beat: atonement through surrender of power.

chapters.title: The Long Route, Reopened
chapters.summary: Beacon by beacon, the haul network comes back online. Adeyemi, recovered, pilots the first civilian run to the repaired relay. Zephyrine rides along, seeing the route as a thread re-stitched. Beat: hope made logistical.

chapters.title: Sebastian and the Protocol
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Zephyrine's POV. Revealed: Sebastian was the founders' name for the protocol itself—the anxious guardian they built instead of trusting their children. Now renamed by Idris, it runs as a library, not a jailer. Zephyrine tends the garden for people who are finally coming. Beat: peace earned, inheritance accepted.
